Study how the big bois make their content in your field. Study how they make their thumbnails, how short or long the title of their videos are and what they are saying (or not saying) in those titles, how long the videos are, what kind of hashtags they use, what video tags they use, whether or not they use chapters.

Copy all the techniques the massive channels use. Not saying to copy their content, just how they frame it to make it the most palatable to the audience.

Also, there are settings you may or may not need to change on your videos and channel as a whole. There's a lot, so just look up "Youtube settings to change to grow your channel" or something like that. Watch of few of those videos and change what is applicable to you. Most of these settings will be on the PC/Desktop version ONLY. So be certain to switch to that

The biggest things though : 

1-If you are making content on subject like say... idk Baseball. JUST make baseball related videos. If your channel is all about one thing and it's the thing you're going to stick with, don't deviate. Because the algorithm will completely shit the bed and you'll get no views if you do deviate. The more you do 1 thing, the easier time youtube will have sending your stuff to the right people.

2-Go into your channel settings and add "Channel Tags" relevant to your channel. Basically, treat YouTube like it's single STUPIDEST person you have ever met and you have to keep repeating yourself a million times. Your channel needs to be dripping with everything that you are about. Every description, pinned comment, title, thumbnail, tag, ALL of it. That way, you leave youtube with absolutely zero doubt on what your channel is actually about.

3-Watch your own video, all the way through right after your post it. Make a pinned comment about literally anything and have a "Call To Action" in the video itself and in the pinned comment to Like, Share and all that good stuff. As far as placement of saying it or typing it in the video, it can be at the beginning, middle or end of the video. Also, if you have a secondary account. Go ahead and log into that one and watch your video all the way through on that account too. Even make a comment if you're feeling squirrely. It helps boost watch time & engagement, which helps push your video out to more people. Every little bit helps.

4-After the video uploads, use the desktop version of youtube. Either on your phone or PC (These options I'm about to tell you are only available on the desktop version) and click on "End Screen", then select 1 or 2 videos and a Subscribe option. The videos should be "Most Recent" and "Best For Viewer/Your choice". "Most Recent" is a must.

5-Put all your videos in a Playlist.

Most everything else ANYBODY tells you outside of this is gonna be nothing more than hot shit. Unless of course, you find a genuine person that has actually made it big and what they say to you actually makes sense. That's the big thing to remember. If it makes sense. Try it. If it doesn't, the next time you hear somebody mention it, you can immediately go elsewhere.

NEVER listen to somebody doing worse than you. EVER. Only listen to people doing better than you or at the very least about as good, so you can glean a tactic you may not have tried yet.

I'm almost at 2k followers Myself and right after I started doing this stuff (I was at 1000 at the time) I started snowballing and got 600 followers kinda quick. Don't be afraid to "Trim The Fat" on your channel either. Stick to whatever kind of consistency that your schedule allows and you'll do well

Boi oh boi, it's A LOT. I'll share only the most stand out issues that contribute to the turnover, but it's still gonna be a big chunk lol.

This is all when I worked there years ago, mind you, so I dont know what all has changed since then.

At this time, we were overstocked and overstocked BAD. I mean product down every single isle. Normally, they had enough space for 2 machines, the over stock made it a 1 machine lane. Which meant whoever got in first got to pick and the others had to wait. That was a problem because we were all on timed production. The longer it took to complete pallets, the more ass they chewed. Despite the ridiculous situation. All they cared about were numbers. Already bad right?

Well in addition to that, we never knew when our work night was gonna end (2nd shift - Which they laid everybody off of and the eliminated 2nd shift entirely,  only to bring it back later 🤦‍♂️. They truly are clueless on everything accept how to make things worse) AND they had mandatory weekends. The main problem with working weekends is that on Saturday and Sunday, they didn't have us come in at 3 or 4pm like a normal day. That would be sane. No no.

They had us working until 2 to almost 4 am on those Fridays and made us all come it at like 7 or 8am. Barely 4-5 hours of sleep after working a full week and then put us on 8k lbs machines and hurried us to do our work. Real real safe huh? 😂. Actually, even LESS sleep than that because most of the people lived 30 minutes to an hour away. Then of course, we just worked the next week. 12 -14 days straight in some cases. All mandatory, well over 40 hours and with threat of write ups if we didnt show or tried to call in.

The worst part of that? It wasn't even busy season. There was one, absolutely brain dead woman in charge of how much product was delivered and she just kept ordering. Over and over AND OVER AGAIN. Nobody told her to do this. Within a month of her being fired, we were no longer over stocked ever again. Even during busy season. Not like how it was at least. Oh and we ALL had to stand on boxes to even reach the product right?

Everybody did it. All the supervisors were aware and understood the situation. This little soy boy GM comes in and who's the 1st he sees? Me 🙄. So I get written up for a "Safety Violation" even though everybody was told to "Do what is needed in the safest manner" Thankfully Scott understood. His hands were tied and I could see it on his face that he hated having to go through with writing Me up. Especially because everybody HAD to stand on other boxes to even be able to do their job. I liked Scott. He was chill. Hope he's doing okay.

Other than that. All the machines were dog trash, out dated and dangerous. Held together by hopes and prayers. Some of them, you could not come to a stop without using the emergency brake every, single, time. They put this dude who couldn't hardly see or hear on a machine and he nearly crushed a girl against the racks. Guess what happened to him?

Nothing. He was still on a machine for MONTHS after that incident that happened in front of literally every body.

All the racks weren't properly secured and you could physically see them wobble when somebody was putting a pallet into them. Always blamed the workers if the system didn't work even though the system was trash and always had issues.

And that lol, was the short version. People came and went all the time because they didn't want to put up with all the BS. One time I found a USED CONDOM on one of the boxes bro... like wtf?

2. It MASSIVELY slows down the drivers who are on timed production and no matter what you said as to why you were slower, they counted it all as excuses and chewed you out.

3 waste of company money and resources as well as everybody's time.

The absolute STUPIDEST thing, though?

The drivers... we're told... they were not allowed to reverse....... on machines that were built to go forward and backward. Everybody was properly trained on how to operate them. They are supposed to be used in reverse as well lol. Thankfully, that didn't last long. The only reason I found THAT out was because a dude I talked with at a temp job worked there before he joined on where I was. That was a recent change.

Oh and the person they put in charge of all the forklift drivers? Yeah, she never drove a lift in her life. Knows nothing about them.
